You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`builder.py` works on a checkout with tools, and the words follow. `Plane` becomes `Tools`, and every `world` in names, parameters, keys, docstrings, comments, messages and the usage line becomes `checkout`: the usage line reads `builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`, the numbers key `world` becomes `checkout`, `world_head` becomes `head` in the numbers and the function that computes it becomes `head()`. In the role text `a world` becomes `a checkout` and nothing else in it changes. The checkout must be a git checkout: a directory without `.git` is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists, so the branches that record `not a git checkout` and a null head go, and `head` is always a commit. `plans` leaves `HIDDEN`. `test_builder.py` already uses the new names; the tests whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour and the rest of the suite must stay green.

380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""

382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()

387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )

428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),

def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

4	
5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.
12	- Walls in the plane: paths outside the world; hidden roots `runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `plans`, `.git`; protected `test*.py`, `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `check.Dockerfile`; 30 writes and edits and 8 checks per run; 80 tool calls and 60 requests in the library.
13	- The check runs `python -P -m unittest discover` because a world-root `unittest.py` would otherwise turn any suite green; the image is built once from the world's own lock, with git because the world's tests use it.
14	- The record grows by `diff.patch` (against HEAD, plus a diff per untracked file), `check-<n>.log`, and numbers for writes, edits, checks, the plane's own verdict on the last check next to the report's claim, and the diff counts. No temperature in the request.
15	- 37 acceptance tests written from the plan before the code; the code written to pass them; an independent review found a writable `.git` and a forgeable green, both closed and pinned.
16	- First runs, after the tag: G1 green in 3 edits and 2 checks ($0.009, 32 s), its diff merged on `main` as commit 48cbbe4, the first change built by the factory (the commit is titled `v0.4` from before that number was given to the gate; the tag `v0.4` includes it); G2, a test that cannot pass, red with no edits and an honest report.
17	
18	## Spec as approved
19	
20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.
21	
22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
31	
32	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
33	
34	## Facts established (2026-09-15)
35	
36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). Unprivileged user namespaces are blocked for unconfined binaries (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1`; `unshare -Urn` fails), so `unshare` and `systemd-run --user` cannot isolate the network. `bubblewrap` is not installed (apt candidate 0.9.0; its AppArmor profile permits userns). uv 0.8.0 with `uv export`. Python 3.12.3.
37	- **Library.** pydantic-ai-slim 2.43.0 as pinned; see `plans/pydantic-ai-facts.md`. A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.
38	- **DeepSeek.** Thinking mode is on by default at effort `high` for `deepseek-flash`. In thinking mode `temperature`, `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty` "will not trigger an error but will also have no effect": our `temperature: 0` in v0.1 and v0.2 did nothing. `reasoning_content` must be passed back on every subsequent request or the API returns 400; the library does this. Profile override from v0.2 kept (upstream issue #8353 open).
39	- **Reference builder prompt.** mini-SWE-agent's system template is one sentence ("You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer."); the work lives in the instance message: the task, a numbered workflow (read relevant files, reproduce, edit, verify, edge cases, submit with an explicit command), and execution rules. Short, structured, task-adjacent, no persona.
40	
41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). Image `factory-check:<12 hex of sha256(uv.lock + check.Dockerfile)>` built once from `check.Dockerfile` (`python:3.12-slim`, `pip install` of `uv export --frozen --no-hashes`), with network; the check itself runs `docker run --rm --network none --user <uid>:<gid> -e HOME=/tmp -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 -v <world>:/w:ro -w /w --memory 1g --cpus 2 --pids-limit 256 <image> python -P -m unittest discover -q`, subprocess timeout 120 s then `docker kill` (30 s). `-P` keeps the world off `sys.path` while the standard runner is imported: without it a world-root `unittest.py` written by the model turns any suite green (review finding, reproduced in the real sandbox). The image build has a `.dockerignore` so the context is the toolchain, not the world's `.venv` and records. Model-written code never runs on the host and cannot reach the key or the network. The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. Alternatives weighed: `bubblewrap` is lighter (no daemon, no image, host venv bind-mounted read-only) and is the better long-term fit, but needs `sudo apt install bubblewrap`; `unshare`/`systemd-run` are blocked by the userns policy; gVisor and Podman are not installed. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.
62	12. **Tags** `v0.3` at the merge. The factory's first build (G1 below) becomes `v0.4` after review, the first version built by the factory.
63	
64	## Files
65	
66	All in `/opt/yellow-robots/factory`, built on the worktree `v0.3` from `main`.

68	- `builder.py` (evolved from `observer.py`, one file, ~480 lines): constants (`HIDDEN`, `PROTECTED`, caps, `CHECK_TIMEOUT`, `CHECK_CMD = ("python", "-m", "unittest", "-q")`, `PRICE`); `ROLE`; `BuildReport` and `render`; `Plane(root, run_dir, hidden, protected)` with `_resolve`, `list`, `read` (from v0.2), `write`, `edit`, `check`, counters (`listed`, `read_paths`, `lines_read`, `written`, `edited`, `checks: list[dict(exit, seconds)]`); `Sandbox` (image name from hashes, `ensure_image(world)`, `run(world, run_dir, n) -> (exit, tail)`); `Wire` (from v0.2); `PROFILE`, `build_agent(plane, key, http_client, model)`; `run(agent, goal)` (from v0.2); `main(argv)`: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`, world resolved and required to exist, run dir under the factory's `runs/`, the record as in v0.2 plus `diff.patch` and `check-<n>.log`.

function.name: list
function.description:
List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

path.description: The directory to list, relative to the world root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.name: final_result
function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),

428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""

432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. 4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself

11	```sh

23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.

def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}
```

47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. 49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""

382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()

387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )

428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.

13	- The check runs `python -P -m unittest discover` because a world-root `unittest.py` would otherwise turn any suite green; the image is built once from the world's own lock, with git because the world's tests use it.
14	- The record grows by `diff.patch` (against HEAD, plus a diff per untracked file), `check-<n>.log`, and numbers for writes, edits, checks, the plane's own verdict on the last check next to the report's claim, and the diff counts. No temperature in the request.
15	- 37 acceptance tests written from the plan before the code; the code written to pass them; an independent review found a writable `.git` and a forgeable green, both closed and pinned.
16	- First runs, after the tag: G1 green in 3 edits and 2 checks ($0.009, 32 s), its diff merged on `main` as commit 48cbbe4, the first change built by the factory (the commit is titled `v0.4` from before that number was given to the gate; the tag `v0.4` includes it); G2, a test that cannot pass, red with no edits and an honest report.

18	## Spec as approved
19	
20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
31	
32	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.

35	
36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). Python 3.12.3.
37	- **Library.** pydantic-ai-slim 2.43.0 as pinned; see `plans/pydantic-ai-facts.md`. A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.
38	- **DeepSeek.** Thinking mode is on by default at effort `high` for `deepseek-flash`. In thinking mode `temperature`, `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty` "will not trigger an error but will also have no effect": our `temperature: 0` in v0.1 and v0.2 did nothing. `reasoning_content` must be passed back on every subsequent request or the API returns 400; the library does this. Profile override from v0.2 kept (upstream issue #8353 open).
39	- **Reference builder prompt.** mini-SWE-agent's system template is one sentence ("You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer."); the work lives in the instance message: the task, a numbered workflow (read relevant files, reproduce, edit, verify, edge cases, submit with an explicit command), and execution rules. Short, structured, task-adjacent, no persona.

41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The image build has a `.dockerignore` so the context is the toolchain, not the world's `.venv` and records. Model-written code never runs on the host and cannot reach the key or the network. The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. Alternatives weighed: `bubblewrap` is lighter (no daemon, no image, host venv bind-mounted read-only) and is the better long-term fit, but needs `sudo apt install bubblewrap`; `unshare`/`systemd-run` are blocked by the userns policy; gVisor and Podman are not installed. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.

You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""

382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):

392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""

418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )

429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a world with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39

15	exit 2, before any record exists, so a build always runs on a known commit. The run record lands
16	under the factory's own `runs/`, never in the world. Five functions, the only things the model
17	can do: `list(path)`; `read(path, start)` (numbered lines, 300 lines or 32,000 bytes per call);
18	`write(path, content)` (create or replace a file, parents created inside the world);
19	`edit(path, old, new)` (replace exactly one occurrence of `old`; zero or many is an error naming
20	the count); `check()` (the world's tests in a container, exit code and the last 60 lines back,

23	the world are the whole specification. Walls, all in the plane: paths outside the world are
24	refused; hidden at the world root: `runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `plans`, `.git`

30	report. The check: `docker run --rm --network none --user <uid>:<gid> -v <world>:/w:ro ...
31	python -P -m unittest discover -q`, in an image built once per world from `check.Dockerfile` and
32	the world's `uv.lock` (`factory-check:<hash>`, git installed because the world's tests use it),
33	120 s timeout then the container is killed. `-P` because a world-root `unittest.py` would
34	otherwise shadow the standard library and turn any suite green. Model-written code never runs on
35	the host and cannot reach the key or the network. Provider DeepSeek `deepseek-flash`, key in
36	`~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` (bare key or one `name=value` line), thinking at the API
37	default; no temperature is sent because DeepSeek ignores it in thinking mode.

```python
def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}
```

317	class Sandbox:
318	    """Where the world's tests run: a container, no network, the world mounted read-only.
319	
320	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the world's own locked dependencies,
321	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
322	    """
323	
324	    @staticmethod
325	    def image(world: Path) -> str:
326	        """The image name for this world: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
327	        h = hashlib.sha256((world / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (world / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
328	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
329	
330	    @staticmethod
331	    def ensure_image(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
332	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
333	        name = Sandbox.image(world)
334	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
335	        if seen.returncode == 0:
336	            return name
337	        built = subprocess.run(
338	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
339	            # factory never runs from inside the world.
340	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(world / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(world)],
341	            capture_output=True,
342	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
343	        )
344	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
345	        if built.returncode != 0:
346	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
347	        return name
348	
349	    @staticmethod
350	    def run(world: Path, run_dir: Path, n: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
351	        """The world's tests, once: the exit code and everything the run printed."""
352	        name = Sandbox.ensure_image(world, run_dir)
353	        container = f"factory-check-{run_dir.name}-{n}"
354	        argv = [
355	            "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", container,
356	            "--network", "none",  # the check cannot reach the key, the provider or the internet
357	            "--user", f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
358	            "-e", "HOME=/tmp",
359	            "-e", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1",  # the world is read-only; do not try to cache
360	            "-v", f"{world}:/w:ro", "-w", "/w",
361	            "--memory", "1g", "--cpus", "2", "--pids-limit", "256",
362	            name, *CHECK_CMD,
363	        ]  # fmt: skip
364	        try:
365	            done = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, timeout=CHECK_TIMEOUT)
366	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
367	            try:  # the check is over either way; a wedged daemon must not hang the run too
368	                subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", container], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
369	            except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
370	                pass
371	            return 124, f"timeout after {CHECK_TIMEOUT} s"
372	        # unittest writes to stderr; the world's own code may write to either.
373	        return done.returncode, (done.stdout + done.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out
411	
412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),
439	        )

518	def dirty_paths(world: Path) -> list[str]:
519	    """The paths a git world has changed, staged or not, as git status names them. Read-only."""
520	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
521	    # Each entry is two status characters, a space, then the path; a rename adds the old path as
522	    # a second NUL-separated field, which does not have that shape and is skipped.
523	    return [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if len(entry) > 3 and entry[2] == " "]

526	def record_diff(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}
530	    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
531	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
532	    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
533	    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too; before the first commit
534	    # there is no HEAD and a bare diff is all there is.
535	    head = subprocess.run(
536	        ["git", "-C", str(world), "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD"],
537	        capture_output=True,
538	        timeout=60,
539	    ).returncode == 0
540	    diff = ["diff", "HEAD"] if head else ["diff"]
541	    patch = [git(world, *diff)]
542	    for rel in untracked:
543	        patch.append(git(world, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
544	    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
545	    files = insertions = deletions = 0
546	    for line in git(world, *diff, "--numstat").splitlines():
547	        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
548	        files += 1
549	        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
550	        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
551	    for rel in untracked:
552	        files += 1
553	        p = world / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
554	        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
555	    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. 31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. 37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39

42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.
12	- Walls in the plane: paths outside the world; hidden roots `runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`, `.venv`, `plans`, `.git`; protected `test*.py`, `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, `check.Dockerfile`; 30 writes and edits and 8 checks per run; 80 tool calls and 60 requests in the library.
13	- The check runs `python -P -m unittest discover` because a world-root `unittest.py` would otherwise turn any suite green; the image is built once from the world's own lock, with git because the world's tests use it.
14	- The record grows by `diff.patch` (against HEAD, plus a diff per untracked file), `check-<n>.log`, and numbers for writes, edits, checks, the plane's own verdict on the last check next to the report's claim, and the diff counts. No temperature in the request.
15	- 37 acceptance tests written from the plan before the code; the code written to pass them; an independent review found a writable `.git` and a forgeable green, both closed and pinned.
16	- First runs, after the tag: G1 green in 3 edits and 2 checks ($0.009, 32 s), its diff merged on `main` as commit 48cbbe4, the first change built by the factory (the commit is titled `v0.4` from before that number was given to the gate; the tag `v0.4` includes it); G2, a test that cannot pass, red with no edits and an honest report.
17	
18	## Spec as approved
19	
20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.
21	
22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
31	
32	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
33

35	
36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). Python 3.12.3.
37	- **Library.** pydantic-ai-slim 2.43.0 as pinned; see `plans/pydantic-ai-facts.md`. A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.

44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. 46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. 48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. 379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out
411	
412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),
439	        )

def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.

10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.

13	- The check runs `python -P -m unittest discover` because a world-root `unittest.py` would otherwise turn any suite green; the image is built once from the world's own lock, with git because the world's tests use it.
14	- The record grows by `diff.patch` (against HEAD, plus a diff per untracked file), `check-<n>.log`, and numbers for writes, edits, checks, the plane's own verdict on the last check next to the report's claim, and the diff counts. No temperature in the request.

18	## Spec as approved

20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
