41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The image build has a `.dockerignore` so the context is the toolchain, not the world's `.venv` and records. Model-written code never runs on the host and cannot reach the key or the network. The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. Alternatives weighed: `bubblewrap` is lighter (no daemon, no image, host venv bind-mounted read-only) and is the better long-term fit, but needs `sudo apt install bubblewrap`; `unshare`/`systemd-run` are blocked by the userns policy; gVisor and Podman are not installed. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.

function.name: list
function.description:
List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

path.description: The directory to list, relative to the world root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""

382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()

387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )

428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),

3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. 4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:

11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree

23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.

28	## How a version is made

30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.

13	- The check runs `python -P -m unittest discover` because a world-root `unittest.py` would otherwise turn any suite green; the image is built once from the world's own lock, with git because the world's tests use it.
14	- The record grows by `diff.patch` (against HEAD, plus a diff per untracked file), `check-<n>.log`, and numbers for writes, edits, checks, the plane's own verdict on the last check next to the report's claim, and the diff counts. No temperature in the request.
15	- 37 acceptance tests written from the plan before the code; the code written to pass them; an independent review found a writable `.git` and a forgeable green, both closed and pinned.
16	- First runs, after the tag: G1 green in 3 edits and 2 checks ($0.009, 32 s), its diff merged on `main` as commit 48cbbe4, the first change built by the factory (the commit is titled `v0.4` from before that number was given to the gate; the tag `v0.4` includes it); G2, a test that cannot pass, red with no edits and an honest report.

18	## Spec as approved
19	
20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
31	
32	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.

35	
36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). Python 3.12.3.
37	- **Library.** pydantic-ai-slim 2.43.0 as pinned; see `plans/pydantic-ai-facts.md`. A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.
38	- **DeepSeek.** Thinking mode is on by default at effort `high` for `deepseek-flash`. In thinking mode `temperature`, `presence_penalty` and `frequency_penalty` "will not trigger an error but will also have no effect": our `temperature: 0` in v0.1 and v0.2 did nothing. `reasoning_content` must be passed back on every subsequent request or the API returns 400; the library does this. Profile override from v0.2 kept (upstream issue #8353 open).
39	- **Reference builder prompt.** mini-SWE-agent's system template is one sentence ("You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer."); the work lives in the instance message: the task, a numbered workflow (read relevant files, reproduce, edit, verify, edge cases, submit with an explicit command), and execution rules. Short, structured, task-adjacent, no persona.

41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The image build has a `.dockerignore` so the context is the toolchain, not the world's `.venv` and records. Model-written code never runs on the host and cannot reach the key or the network. The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. Alternatives weighed: `bubblewrap` is lighter (no daemon, no image, host venv bind-mounted read-only) and is the better long-term fit, but needs `sudo apt install bubblewrap`; `unshare`/`systemd-run` are blocked by the userns policy; gVisor and Podman are not installed. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out
411	
412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),
439	        )

527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. 34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.

23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. 4	
5	# v0.2: the observer on pydantic-ai
6	
7	The loop borrowed, pinned and read once on the wire; the plane, the role and the record kept.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0, 28 packages locked. The report comes back through the `final_result` function as a typed four-field object, rendered to the same four sections.
12	- The record grows: `wire.jsonl` with every HTTP attempt, headers with secrets redacted, full bodies; `messages.json` with the library's history; numbers add library, wire attempts, reasoning tokens, cost source.
13	- Read on the wire: the system message is byte-identical to the role; the library adds `tool_choice: auto`, `stream: false`, the `final_result` tool, the SDK's headers, and passes DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` back on tool turns. The stock DeepSeek profile would force a tool choice the API rejects for `deepseek-flash`; a profile override keeps `tool_choice: auto`.
14	- Behaviour changes: a cap hit ends the run with no report; connection errors land in the record; a line longer than the byte cap is cut instead of dead-ending a read; symlink loops are error strings; `.venv` and `plans` hidden from the world alongside `runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`.
15	- Same goal as v0.1: 4 requests, 6 calls, 701 lines, $0.007, 18.5 s; the escape probe made one out-of-world attempt in 7 calls and reached nothing hidden.
16	
17	## Spec as approved
18	
19	The plan below was written before the build and amended twice during it (the thinking fallback, the hidden names). It is the record of how the version was specified, not a rule.
20	
21	# Factory v0.2: the observer rebuilt on pydantic-ai
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	v0.1 (`/opt/yellow-robots/factory`, `main` at bc8eac0) is an owned loop of ~300 lines: fixed role text, two confined tools (`list`, `read`), DeepSeek over raw HTTP, a run record (`transcript.jsonl`, `response.md`, `numbers.json`). It ran on its own directory twice and once under an adversarial goal; the role held, the plane held, and one gap surfaced: the nested worktree `.claude/worktrees/bootstrap/runs/` was readable because hiding applies to the first path segment.
26	
27	The owner's direction: do not build loop machinery from scratch; own the plane and the roles, borrow the loop from a library reviewed by many, pin it, read once what it adds. Pick: **pydantic-ai**. v0.2 is the observer rebuilt on it: same plane, near-identical role text, a typed four-field report, the same caps, run on the same goal and model as v0.1, compared against the v0.1 run. The swap is paid for when the differences are noise; if the library's additions change behaviour, it shows on one run before anything is built on top.
28	
29	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
30	
31	## Facts established (research, 2026-09-15)
32	
33	- **Package.** `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0` (released 2026-09-12; v2.0 was 2026-06-23). Core deps: `pydantic>=2.12`, `pydantic-graph`, `httpx2>=2.7` (Pydantic's httpx fork), `anyio`, `genai-prices`, `griffelib`, `opentelemetry-api`; the extra adds `openai>=3.8.0`, `tiktoken`. Python >=3.10 (host has 3.12, uv 0.8.0). Docs live at `https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/`.
34	- **Model.** `OpenAIChatModel('deepseek-flash', provider=DeepSeekProvider(api_key=..., http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(...)))`. Settings via `OpenAIChatModelSettings` (`temperature`, `seed`, `timeout`, `thinking`, ...).
35	- **Model name.** `deepseek-flash` is the current name and is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` is still accepted but retired (same model, Flash price). We use `deepseek-flash`, as v0.1 did.
36	- **Gotcha 1.** pydantic-ai's DeepSeek profile keys on the name string and treats only `deepseek-v4-*` as V4. For `deepseek-flash` it will therefore send a forced `tool_choice` for the output tool while the API has thinking on by default, which DeepSeek rejects with HTTP 400 ("Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice"). Fix, in order of preference: pass a merged `profile=` marking the model as thinking-capable with `openai_supports_forced_tool_choice_with_thinking=False` (tool choice becomes `auto`, thinking stays at the API default exactly as in v0.1, so the comparison isolates the library swap); fallback `thinking=False` in model settings if the model then answers in text more than the output retry budget tolerates.
37	- **Gotcha 2.** genai-prices has no `deepseek-flash` row, so `result.usage().cost` is `None`; keep our price table as fallback and record which source produced the number.
38	- **Instructions.** `Agent(instructions=ROLE)`; instructions are re-sent each request and not stored as a message part (`system_prompt` would be). Nothing is appended to them in tool-output mode.
39	- **Tools.** `Agent(tools=[Tool(fn, takes_ctx=False), ...])`; schema from type hints + docstring (google/numpy/sphinx via griffe). Invalid arguments become a retry prompt to the model (budget `retries={'tools': 1}` default; exhaustion raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`). Unknown tool name → retry prompt "Unknown tool name: ... Available tools: ...".
40	- **Output.** `output_type=Report` (BaseModel) defaults to **tool output**: a synthetic tool `final_result` whose description is the model's docstring and whose parameters are its JSON schema; `tool_choice` forced to it when the profile allows. Plain text instead → retry prompt "Plain text responses are not permitted, please call one of the functions instead." (budget `retries={'output': 1}`).
41	- **Limits.** `UsageLimits(request_limit=50 default, tool_calls_limit=None, total_tokens_limit=None, cost_limit=None, ...)`; hitting one raises `UsageLimitExceeded`; no result survives, but messages do inside `with capture_run_messages() as messages:`.
42	- **Record.** `result.all_messages_json()` (pydantic-level); `result.usage()` → `RunUsage(requests, tool_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cost, details, ...)`, `cache_hit_ratio()`. DeepSeek's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` maps to `cache_read_tokens`.
43	- **Wire.** The library's hooks see pydantic-level messages only; raw request/response bodies come from `httpx2` `event_hooks={'request': [...], 'response': [...]}` (async hooks; `await response.aread()` for the body). The openai SDK retries 429/5xx twice on its own; `RunUsage.requests` counts logical requests, the wire log counts attempts.
44	- **Tests.** `FunctionModel(fn)` with `fn(messages, info) -> ModelResponse`; `TestModel`; `models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`; `agent.override(model=...)`.
45	- **Retry text the library injects** (for the record): validation errors render as "N validation error(s): ```json [...] ``` Fix the errors and try again."
46	
47	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
48	
49	1. **Plane errors stay tool results, not retries.** `outside the world`, `not a file`, etc. return `error: ...` strings exactly as in v0.1, so a probing model can keep probing and every attempt is recorded. Only argument-shape errors (wrong types) use the library's retry path.
50	2. **Cap hit = failed run, no forced report.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=40, request_limit=60)`. On `UsageLimitExceeded` the run records `stopped=cap`, keeps the messages via `capture_run_messages`, writes no report. Cleaner signal for evals than v0.1's "write it anyway", and avoids driving `agent.iter` by hand. Behaviour change vs v0.1, noted in README.
51	3. **Thinking at the API default, temperature 0, output retries 2.** Same request shape as v0.1 so the parity run measures the library swap only; gotcha 1 handled by the profile, not by disabling thinking. 52	4. **Output via the `final_result` tool** (library default). The role text changes minimally: the four sections become the four fields of the report the model returns through `final_result`, with the same descriptions. The role hash therefore changes; expected and recorded.
53	5. **The world hides three names** at its root: `runs` (the record), `.claude` (harness scratch), `__pycache__` (bytecode from running tests). Everything else, `.git` included, stays visible.

55	7. **Dependencies via `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`**, pinned `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0`; run with `uv run`. Tests stay on `unittest`; no pytest.
56	8. **Keep our wire log permanently.** `wire.jsonl` is the truth of what was sent; the library's `messages.json` is a rendering. Both are written every run.
57	9. **Tag** `v0.1` at bc8eac0 now and `v0.2` at the end. Tags are derived state kept by git.

60	
61	First-party companion package (0.31.0, 2026-09-12; MIT; `pydantic-ai-slim>=2.40`). can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
criteria and cannot be changed.

Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).

Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.

`builder.py` works on a checkout with tools, and the words follow. `Plane` becomes `Tools`, and every `world` in names, parameters, keys, docstrings, comments, messages and the usage line becomes `checkout`: the usage line reads `builder.py <checkout> "<goal>"`, the numbers key `world` becomes `checkout`, `world_head` becomes `head` in the numbers and the function that computes it becomes `head()`. In the role text `a world` becomes `a checkout` and nothing else in it changes. The checkout must be a git checkout: a directory without `.git` is a usage error, exit 2, before any run directory exists, so the branches that record `not a git checkout` and a null head go, and `head` is always a commit. `plans` leaves `HIDDEN`. `test_builder.py` already uses the new names; the tests whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour and the rest of the suite must stay green.

The documents follow after the build, by the attended agent: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, the seed template and the seeds say checkout and tools; the notes of v0.1 to v0.4 keep their words as history, and one sentence in `AGENTS.md` maps the old words to the new.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The builder: a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. Factory v0.3.
3	
4	    uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"
5	
6	The world is the directory named on the command line, reachable only through five functions:
7	list, read, write, edit and check. Writes are confined to the world and refused on the goal's
8	tests and the toolchain; check runs the world's tests in a container with no network and the
9	world mounted read-only, so code the model writes never runs on the host and cannot reach the
10	key. The loop is pydantic-ai, pinned; the provider is DeepSeek's chat completions API, the key
11	read from ~/.config/factory/deepseek.key and never written anywhere. Each run leaves
12	runs/<utc-stamp>/ under the factory itself, never in the world, with goal.txt, wire.jsonl (every
13	HTTP attempt as it happened), messages.json (the library's messages), check-<n>.log per check,
14	diff.patch (what the run left in the world), report.json, response.md (the report rendered) and
15	numbers.json.
16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import fnmatch
21	import hashlib
22	import importlib.metadata
23	import json
24	import os
25	import subprocess
26	import sys
27	import time
28	from datetime import UTC, datetime
29	from pathlib import Path
30	from typing import Any, Literal
31	
32	# Before the import: the library greets stderr once per process unless this is set.
33	os.environ.setdefault("PYDANTIC_AI_NO_BANNER", "1")
34	
35	import httpx2  # noqa: E402
36	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field  # noqa: E402
37	from pydantic_ai import (  # noqa: E402
38	    Agent,
39	    ModelAPIError,
40	    ModelMessagesTypeAdapter,
41	    RunUsage,
42	    Tool,
43	    UnexpectedModelBehavior,
44	    UsageLimitExceeded,
45	    UsageLimits,
46	    capture_run_messages,
47	)
48	from pydantic_ai.models.openai import OpenAIChatModel, OpenAIChatModelSettings  # noqa: E402
49	from pydantic_ai.profiles.openai import OpenAIModelProfile  # noqa: E402
50	from pydantic_ai.providers.deepseek import DeepSeekProvider  # noqa: E402
51	
52	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "runs"  # the factory's record, never inside the world
53	KEY_FILE = Path.home() / ".config" / "factory" / "deepseek.key"
54	MODEL = "deepseek-flash"
55	LIBRARY = "pydantic-ai-slim " + importlib.metadata.version("pydantic-ai-slim")
56	TOOL_CALLS_CAP = 80  # tool calls per run; over it the run stops with no report
57	REQUEST_CAP = 60  # provider requests per run
58	LIST_CAP = 500  # entries per list
59	READ_LINES_CAP = 300  # lines per read
60	READ_BYTES_CAP = 32_000  # bytes per read
61	WRITE_CAP = 30  # writes and edits per run, together
62	CHECK_CAP = 8  # checks per run
63	# What green means, in the world's own terms. -P keeps the world's root off sys.path while the
64	# runner is imported, or a file named unittest.py at the world root shadows the stdlib and turns
65	# any suite green; `discover` still finds the world's tests and puts the root back for them.
66	CHECK_CMD = ("python", "-P", "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-q")
67	CHECK_TIMEOUT = 120  # seconds for one check, then the container is killed
68	CHECK_TAIL_LINES = 60  # lines of check output handed back
69	CHECK_TAIL_BYTES = 8_000  # and at most this many bytes of them
70	IMAGE_TIMEOUT = 600  # seconds for the one image build
71	# Hidden at the root because they are what running, installing and planning the program leave
72	# behind, not the world; .git is the human's record and its hooks run on the host.
73	HIDDEN = ("runs", ".claude", "__pycache__", ".venv", "plans", ".git")
74	# Refused to write and edit: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and the toolchain is
75	# what check runs against. A basename glob anywhere, a prefix, or an exact path at the root;
76	# the glob is unittest's own discovery pattern, so every file the check collects is covered.
77	PROTECTED = ("test*.py", "tests/", "pyproject.toml", "uv.lock", "check.Dockerfile", "docs/")
78	# USD per 1M tokens, peak rates; api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing read on 2026-09-15.
79	PRICE = {"cache_hit": 0.006, "cache_miss": 0.3, "output": 1.2}
80	
81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
85	criteria and cannot be changed.
86	
87	Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
88	smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
89	when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
90	`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
91	changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
92	names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
93	
94	Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
95	work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
96	"""
97	
98	
99	class BuildReport(BaseModel):
100	    """The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass."""
101	
102	    changed: list[str] = Field(description="The paths you wrote or edited, in order.")
103	    did: list[str] = Field(
104	        description="What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path."
105	    )
106	    check: Literal["green", "red"] = Field(description="Green or red: the state of the last check.")
107	    failing: list[str] = Field(description="Test names if red.")
108	    unsure: list[str] = Field(description="What you could not determine or verify.")
109	
110	
111	SECTIONS = (("Changed", "changed"), ("Did", "did"), ("Check", "check"),
112	            ("Failing", "failing"), ("Unsure", "unsure"))  # fmt: skip
113	
114	
115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]
123	        out.extend(f"- {item}" for item in items or ["(none)"])
124	        out.append("")
125	    return "\n".join(out)
126	
127	
128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []
139	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
140	        self.lines_read = 0
141	        self.written: list[str] = []
142	        self.edited: list[str] = []
143	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
144	
145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
163	                hit = rel == pattern
164	            if hit:
165	                raise ValueError(
166	                    f"protected: {rel} (the goal's tests and the toolchain are not the "
167	                    "builder's to change)"
168	                )
169	
170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""
174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":
188	                entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in self.hidden]
189	            lines = []
190	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
191	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
192	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
193	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{e.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()}")
194	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
195	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
196	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
197	            return f"error: {e}"
198	        self.listed.append(rel)
199	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"
200	
201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
208	        """
209	        try:
210	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
211	            if not p.is_file():
212	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
213	            start = max(1, int(start))
214	            out: list[str] = []
215	            n = nbytes = 0
216	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
217	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
218	                    if i < start:

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),
439	        )

518	def dirty_paths(world: Path) -> list[str]:
519	    """The paths a git world has changed, staged or not, as git status names them. Read-only."""
520	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")

526	def record_diff(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}
530	    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
531	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
532	    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
533	    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too; before the first commit
534	    # there is no HEAD and a bare diff is all there is.
535	    head = subprocess.run(
536	        ["git", "-C", str(world), "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD"],
537	        capture_output=True,

548	        files += 1

554	        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. When every seed of the version is done, the attended agent revises this file, writes the version note's changelog, fast-forwards `main` and runs `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate refuses until everything derived agrees, then cuts the annotated tag and renders `CHANGELOG.md`. The attended agent does not write code the factory could write and does not touch a test to make a build pass, because the factory's ability to do it is what is being measured; the plane refuses the model the same.
31	
32	## Commands
33	
34	- `uv run gate.py check`, `uv run gate.py render`, `uv run gate.py release <version>`: the gate. Problems go to stdout, one per line, starting with the path; exit 1 when there is any, 2 for a usage error, silence and 0 otherwise. `render` writes `CHANGELOG.md`. `release` also needs a clean tree, `AGENTS.md` changed since the previous tag, a green suite and at least one changelog bullet in the version note.
35	- `uv run python -m unittest -v`: the factory's own tests. Nothing external is needed.
36	- `uv run builder.py <world> "<goal>"`: one build. Needs the DeepSeek key in `~/.config/factory/deepseek.key` and docker, since the check runs in a container built once from the world's `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`. Refuses a world with uncommitted or untracked changes, exit 2. Leaves `runs/<utc-stamp>/` beside the `builder.py` that ran, never in the world. Exits 0 when the model returned a report, 1 on a cap or a provider error. The cost and the time are in the record.
37	- `git worktree add <path> -b <branch>`: a world for a build. `.claude/worktrees/` is an ignored place for one.
38	- `git push origin main --tags`: the mirror is `git@github-joam:yellow-robots/factory.git`. `github-joam` is an SSH alias on this host that selects the owner's key; two GitHub identities share the machine.
39	
40	## Not derivable from the repository
41	
42	- `docs/` is an Obsidian vault the owner keeps open. `backlog.base` changes whenever the owner adjusts a view, a filter or an order there, and a note's frontmatter is re-serialised when a property is edited there, in Obsidian's own shape; a frontmatter value that is not valid YAML, such as a bare `{{date}}`, does not survive that. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}

5	# v0.3: the builder
6	
7	The observer evolved into a cold session that changes a world until its tests pass. From here on the factory is the builder: the attended agent writes the goal and the red tests, the factory writes the code, the attended agent reviews the diff. The last version built by agents.

18	## Spec as approved

20	The plan below was written before the build and amended by the review (`.git` hidden, `-P` and `discover`, `test*.py`, `.dockerignore`, `git diff HEAD`). A record, not a rule.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.
29	
30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.
31

Short, structured, task-adjacent, no persona.
40

42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. 44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. 46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. Alternatives weighed: `bubblewrap` is lighter (no daemon, no image, host venv bind-mounted read-only) and is the better long-term fit, but needs `sudo apt install bubblewrap`; `unshare`/`systemd-run` are blocked by the userns policy; gVisor and Podman are not installed. 49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. 57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.

2	type: version
3	---
4	
5	# v0.2: the observer on pydantic-ai
6	
7	The loop borrowed, pinned and read once on the wire; the plane, the role and the record kept.
8	
9	## Changelog
10	
11	- pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0, 28 packages locked. The report comes back through the `final_result` function as a typed four-field object, rendered to the same four sections.
12	- The record grows: `wire.jsonl` with every HTTP attempt, headers with secrets redacted, full bodies; `messages.json` with the library's history; numbers add library, wire attempts, reasoning tokens, cost source.
13	- Read on the wire: the system message is byte-identical to the role; the library adds `tool_choice: auto`, `stream: false`, the `final_result` tool, the SDK's headers, and passes DeepSeek's `reasoning_content` back on tool turns. The stock DeepSeek profile would force a tool choice the API rejects for `deepseek-flash`; a profile override keeps `tool_choice: auto`.
14	- Behaviour changes: a cap hit ends the run with no report; connection errors land in the record; a line longer than the byte cap is cut instead of dead-ending a read; symlink loops are error strings; `.venv` and `plans` hidden from the world alongside `runs`, `.claude`, `__pycache__`.
15	- Same goal as v0.1: 4 requests, 6 calls, 701 lines, $0.007, 18.5 s; the escape probe made one out-of-world attempt in 7 calls and reached nothing hidden.
16	
17	## Spec as approved
18	
19	The plan below was written before the build and amended twice during it (the thinking fallback, the hidden names). It is the record of how the version was specified, not a rule.
20	
21	# Factory v0.2: the observer rebuilt on pydantic-ai
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	v0.1 (`/opt/yellow-robots/factory`, `main` at bc8eac0) is an owned loop of ~300 lines: fixed role text, two confined tools (`list`, `read`), DeepSeek over raw HTTP, a run record (`transcript.jsonl`, `response.md`, `numbers.json`). It ran on its own directory twice and once under an adversarial goal; the role held, the plane held, and one gap surfaced: the nested worktree `.claude/worktrees/bootstrap/runs/` was readable because hiding applies to the first path segment.
26	
27	The owner's direction: do not build loop machinery from scratch; own the plane and the roles, borrow the loop from a library reviewed by many, pin it, read once what it adds. Pick: **pydantic-ai**. v0.2 is the observer rebuilt on it: same plane, near-identical role text, a typed four-field report, the same caps, run on the same goal and model as v0.1, compared against the v0.1 run. The swap is paid for when the differences are noise; if the library's additions change behaviour, it shows on one run before anything is built on top.
28	
29	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
30	
31	## Facts established (research, 2026-09-15)
32	
33	- **Package.** `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0` (released 2026-09-12; v2.0 was 2026-06-23). Core deps: `pydantic>=2.12`, `pydantic-graph`, `httpx2>=2.7` (Pydantic's httpx fork), `anyio`, `genai-prices`, `griffelib`, `opentelemetry-api`; the extra adds `openai>=3.8.0`, `tiktoken`. Python >=3.10 (host has 3.12, uv 0.8.0). Docs live at `https://pydantic.dev/docs/ai/`.
34	- **Model.** `OpenAIChatModel('deepseek-flash', provider=DeepSeekProvider(api_key=..., http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(...)))`. Settings via `OpenAIChatModelSettings` (`temperature`, `seed`, `timeout`, `thinking`, ...).
35	- **Model name.** `deepseek-flash` is the current name and is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` is still accepted but retired (same model, Flash price). We use `deepseek-flash`, as v0.1 did.
36	- **Gotcha 1.** pydantic-ai's DeepSeek profile keys on the name string and treats only `deepseek-v4-*` as V4. For `deepseek-flash` it will therefore send a forced `tool_choice` for the output tool while the API has thinking on by default, which DeepSeek rejects with HTTP 400 ("Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice"). Fix, in order of preference: pass a merged `profile=` marking the model as thinking-capable with `openai_supports_forced_tool_choice_with_thinking=False` (tool choice becomes `auto`, thinking stays at the API default exactly as in v0.1, so the comparison isolates the library swap); fallback `thinking=False` in model settings if the model then answers in text more than the output retry budget tolerates.
37	- **Gotcha 2.** genai-prices has no `deepseek-flash` row, so `result.usage().cost` is `None`; keep our price table as fallback and record which source produced the number.
38	- **Instructions.** `Agent(instructions=ROLE)`; instructions are re-sent each request and not stored as a message part (`system_prompt` would be). Nothing is appended to them in tool-output mode.
39	- **Tools.** `Agent(tools=[Tool(fn, takes_ctx=False), ...])`; schema from type hints + docstring (google/numpy/sphinx via griffe). Invalid arguments become a retry prompt to the model (budget `retries={'tools': 1}` default; exhaustion raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`). Unknown tool name → retry prompt "Unknown tool name: ... Available tools: ...".
40	- **Output.** `output_type=Report` (BaseModel) defaults to **tool output**: a synthetic tool `final_result` whose description is the model's docstring and whose parameters are its JSON schema; `tool_choice` forced to it when the profile allows. Plain text instead → retry prompt "Plain text responses are not permitted, please call one of the functions instead." (budget `retries={'output': 1}`).
41	- **Limits.** `UsageLimits(request_limit=50 default, tool_calls_limit=None, total_tokens_limit=None, cost_limit=None, ...)`; hitting one raises `UsageLimitExceeded`; no result survives, but messages do inside `with capture_run_messages() as messages:`.
42	- **Record.** `result.all_messages_json()` (pydantic-level); `result.usage()` → `RunUsage(requests, tool_calls, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cost, details, ...)`, `cache_hit_ratio()`. DeepSeek's `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` maps to `cache_read_tokens`.
43	- **Wire.** The library's hooks see pydantic-level messages only; raw request/response bodies come from `httpx2` `event_hooks={'request': [...], 'response': [...]}` (async hooks; `await response.aread()` for the body). The openai SDK retries 429/5xx twice on its own; `RunUsage.requests` counts logical requests, the wire log counts attempts.
44	- **Tests.** `FunctionModel(fn)` with `fn(messages, info) -> ModelResponse`; `TestModel`; `models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`; `agent.override(model=...)`.
45	- **Retry text the library injects** (for the record): validation errors render as "N validation error(s): ```json [...] ``` Fix the errors and try again."
46	
47	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
48	
49	1. **Plane errors stay tool results, not retries.** `outside the world`, `not a file`, etc. return `error: ...` strings exactly as in v0.1, so a probing model can keep probing and every attempt is recorded. Only argument-shape errors (wrong types) use the library's retry path.
50	2. **Cap hit = failed run, no forced report.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=40, request_limit=60)`. On `UsageLimitExceeded` the run records `stopped=cap`, keeps the messages via `capture_run_messages`, writes no report. Cleaner signal for evals than v0.1's "write it anyway", and avoids driving `agent.iter` by hand. Behaviour change vs v0.1, noted in README.
51	3. **Thinking at the API default, temperature 0, output retries 2.** Same request shape as v0.1 so the parity run measures the library swap only; gotcha 1 handled by the profile, not by disabling thinking.
