52	4. **Output via the `final_result` tool** (library default). The role text changes minimally: the four sections become the four fields of the report the model returns through `final_result`, with the same descriptions. The role hash therefore changes; expected and recorded.
53	5. **The world hides three names** at its root: `runs` (the record), `.claude` (harness scratch), `__pycache__` (bytecode from running tests). Everything else, `.git` included, stays visible.
54	6. **Remove the nested worktree** `.claude/worktrees/bootstrap` (branches `bootstrap` and `v0.1` are both mirrored on GitHub) after copying its first-ever run `runs/20260915T085903Z` into the main checkout's `runs/`. Closes the gap the adversarial run found at the source, not only by hiding.
55	7. **Dependencies via `pyproject.toml` + `uv.lock`**, pinned `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0`; run with `uv run`. Tests stay on `unittest`; no pytest.
56	8. **Keep our wire log permanently.** `wire.jsonl` is the truth of what was sent; the library's `messages.json` is a rendering. Both are written every run.
57	9. **Tag** `v0.1` at bc8eac0 now and `v0.2` at the end. Tags are derived state kept by git.
58	
59	## Considered and not used in v0.2: `pydantic-ai-harness`
60	
61	First-party companion package (0.31.0, 2026-09-12; MIT; `pydantic-ai-slim>=2.40`). Fifty-plus composable capabilities: `FileSystem(root, read_only=...)` with read/write/edit/search tools and path-traversal/symlink safety, `Shell` with allowlists, `RepoContext` (injects `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` and repo structure), `Planning`, `Memory`, `SubAgents`, `Compaction`, guardrails, and the prebuilt `Coder` and `Researcher` agents. Each capability is usable alone via `Agent(capabilities=[...])`.
62	
63	Not used now, for three reasons:
64	
65	- **It is the stack v0.1 deliberately did not assume.** Shell, repo-orientation prose, planning files and memory are exactly the capabilities and narrated state we removed; the factory grants one function per version and measures it. Nothing in the harness is off the table forever, but each piece enters only when a version's goal needs it.
66	- **The plane is the factory's design surface, not plumbing.** What the model can do to the world, how results are shaped (numbered lines, truncation continuation), what is hidden, and what is counted are the thing under study. v0.2 changes one variable, the loop; swapping the plane in the same version would blur the comparison.
67	- **0.x versioning**: APIs move between minor releases, three months after pydantic-ai 2.0. The core library carries the stability pledge; the harness does not yet.
68	
69	Where it does earn a look, as its own version: `FileSystem(read_only=True)` against our two functions on the same goals, judged by the runs (its path safety is reviewed code for exactly what we hand-wrote), and later `FileSystem` write/edit when a version first needs a write, since atomic edits, encoding and size limits are where reviewed code beats ours. `RepoContext`, `Planning`, `Memory` and `Coder` stay out on principle, not on maturity.
70

1	---
2	type: seed
3	status: done
4	summary: A run is comparable and reproducible only if the world it ran on is a known commit; record it and refuse a dirty world.

9	
10	## Evidence
11	
12	The two builder runs of 2026-09-15 ran on worktrees whose commit is known only from the shell history; `numbers.json` holds the world path, not the commit. The evals (`failure-mode-set`, `variance-runs`) need two runs of one case to be on the same world. The refusal is a wall for the attended agent, not for the model: it forces the tests to be committed before a build.
13	
14	## Goal
15	
16	`builder.py` records the world's `HEAD` commit as `world_head` in `numbers.json`. When the world is a git checkout with uncommitted or untracked changes, it exits 2 with a usage error naming the first dirty paths, before any run directory is created. A world that is not a git checkout records `world_head` as null and runs. Read-only git from the factory side, as `record_diff` already does. The tests in `test_builder.py` whose docstring names this seed define the behaviour.

function.name: list
function.description:
List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

path.description: The directory to list, relative to the world root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

function.name: final_result
function.description: The builder's report: what it changed in the world, and whether the tests pass.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

81	ROLE = """\
82	You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You
83	can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with
84	`check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance
85	criteria and cannot be changed.
86	
87	Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the
88	smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or
89	when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the
90	`final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you
91	changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test
92	names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
93	
94	Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never
95	work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
96	"""

115	def render(report: BuildReport) -> str:
116	    """The report in v0.1's markdown shape: five headings, one bullet per item."""
117	    out: list[str] = []
118	    for heading, field in SECTIONS:
119	        out.append(f"## {heading}")
120	        items = getattr(report, field)
121	        if isinstance(items, str):  # check is one value, and renders as one bullet
122	            items = [items]

128	class Plane:
129	    """The execution plane: what the model can do to the world, and the record of it."""
130	
131	    def __init__(self, root: Path, run_dir: Path, hidden: tuple[str, ...] = HIDDEN,
132	                 protected: tuple[str, ...] = PROTECTED, sandbox: Any = None):  # fmt: skip
133	        self.root = root.resolve()
134	        self.run_dir = run_dir
135	        self.hidden = hidden
136	        self.protected = protected
137	        self.sandbox = sandbox
138	        self.listed: list[str] = []
139	        self.read_paths: list[str] = []
140	        self.lines_read = 0
141	        self.written: list[str] = []
142	        self.edited: list[str] = []
143	        self.checks: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
144	
145	    def _resolve(self, path: str) -> tuple[Path, str]:
146	        p = (self.root / (path or ".")).resolve()
147	        if p != self.root and self.root not in p.parents:
148	            raise ValueError(f"outside the world: {path}")
149	        rel = p.relative_to(self.root).as_posix() or "."
150	        if rel.split("/", 1)[0] in self.hidden:
151	            raise ValueError(f"not part of the world: {path}")
152	        return p, rel
153	
154	    def _writable(self, rel: str) -> None:
155	        """The goal's tests and the toolchain are the human's; the builder may read them only."""
156	        name = rel.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
157	        for pattern in self.protected:
158	            if pattern.endswith("/"):  # anything under that directory
159	                hit = rel == pattern[:-1] or rel.startswith(pattern)
160	            elif "*" in pattern:  # that basename, anywhere in the world
161	                hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern)
162	            else:  # that exact path at the root, not the basename anywhere
163	                hit = rel == pattern
164	            if hit:
165	                raise ValueError(
166	                    f"protected: {rel} (the goal's tests and the toolchain are not the "
167	                    "builder's to change)"
168	                )
169	
170	    def _capped(self) -> str:
171	        if len(self.written) + len(self.edited) >= WRITE_CAP:
172	            return f"error: cap reached ({WRITE_CAP} writes and edits); report now"
173	        return ""
174	
175	    def list(self, path: str = ".") -> str:
176	        """List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
177	        relative to the world root; '.' is the root.
178	
179	        Args:
180	            path: The directory to list, relative to the world root.
181	        """
182	        try:
183	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
184	            if not p.is_dir():
185	                raise ValueError(f"not a directory: {path}")
186	            entries = sorted(p.iterdir(), key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name))
187	            if rel == ".":
188	                entries = [e for e in entries if e.name not in self.hidden]
189	            lines = []
190	            for e in entries[:LIST_CAP]:
191	                kind = "link" if e.is_symlink() else "dir" if e.is_dir() else "file"
192	                size = e.lstat().st_size if kind == "file" else 0
193	                lines.append(f"{kind}\t{size}\t{e.relative_to(self.root).as_posix()}")
194	            if len(entries) > LIST_CAP:
195	                lines.append(f"...\t{len(entries) - LIST_CAP} more entries not shown")
196	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
197	            return f"error: {e}"
198	        self.listed.append(rel)
199	        return "\n".join(lines) or "(empty)"
200	
201	    def read(self, path: str, start: int = 1) -> str:
202	        """Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
203	        lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.
204	
205	        Args:
206	            path: The file to read, relative to the world root.
207	            start: The first line to read, 1-based.
208	        """
209	        try:
210	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
211	            if not p.is_file():
212	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
213	            start = max(1, int(start))
214	            out: list[str] = []
215	            n = nbytes = 0
216	            with p.open("r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f:
217	                for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
218	                    if i < start:
219	                        continue
220	                    size = len(line.encode())
221	                    if n >= READ_LINES_CAP or nbytes + size > READ_BYTES_CAP:
222	                        if n:  # one line per call at least, or a long line dead-ends the read
223	                            out.append(f"...\ttruncated; continue with start={i}")
224	                            break
225	                        cut = line.encode()[:READ_BYTES_CAP].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
226	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{cut} …(line cut at {READ_BYTES_CAP} bytes)")
227	                    else:
228	                        out.append(f"{i}\t{line.rstrip(chr(10))}")
229	                    n += 1
230	                    nbytes += size
231	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
232	            return f"error: {e}"
233	        self.read_paths.append(rel)
234	        self.lines_read += n
235	        return "\n".join(out) or "(empty)"
236	
237	    def write(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
238	        """Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.
239	        Directories on the way are created. The tests and the toolchain cannot be written.
240	
241	        Args:
242	            path: The file to write, relative to the world root.
243	            content: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.
244	        """
245	        capped = self._capped()
246	        if capped:
247	            return capped
248	        try:
249	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
250	            self._writable(rel)
251	            p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
252	            p.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
253	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # RuntimeError: a symlink loop
254	            return f"error: {e}"
255	        self.written.append(rel)
256	        return f"wrote {rel} ({len(content.splitlines())} lines)"
257	
258	    def edit(self, path: str, old: str, new: str) -> str:
259	        """Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
260	        file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
261	        tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.
262	
263	        Args:
264	            path: The file to edit, relative to the world root.
265	            old: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.
266	            new: The text to put in its place.
267	        """
268	        capped = self._capped()
269	        if capped:
270	            return capped
271	        if not old:  # every file contains the empty string, everywhere
272	            return "error: old text is empty"
273	        try:
274	            p, rel = self._resolve(path)
275	            self._writable(rel)
276	            if not p.is_file():
277	                raise ValueError(f"not a file: {path}")
278	            text = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
279	            found = text.count(old)
280	            if found != 1:
281	                if found == 0:
282	                    return f"error: old text not found in {rel}"
283	                return f"error: old text found {found} times in {rel}; include more context"
284	            before = len(text.splitlines())
285	            text = text.replace(old, new, 1)
286	            p.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
287	        except (ValueError, OSError, RuntimeError) as e:  # UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError
288	            return f"error: {e}"
289	        self.edited.append(rel)
290	        return f"edited {rel} ({before} -> {len(text.splitlines())} lines)"
291	
292	    def check(self) -> str:
293	        """Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
294	        green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
295	        no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.
296	        """
297	        if len(self.checks) >= CHECK_CAP:
298	            return f"error: cap reached ({CHECK_CAP} checks); report now"
299	        if self.sandbox is None:
300	            return "error: no sandbox; check is not available in this run"
...	truncated; continue with start=301

301	        n = len(self.checks) + 1
302	        t0 = time.time()
303	        try:
304	            code, output = self.sandbox.run(self.root, self.run_dir, n)
305	            seconds = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
306	            log = self.run_dir / f"check-{n}.log"
307	            log.write_text(output, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
308	        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as e:
309	            return f"error: {e}"
310	        self.checks.append({"exit": code, "seconds": seconds})
311	        tail = "\n".join(output.splitlines()[-CHECK_TAIL_LINES:])
312	        if len(tail.encode()) > CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:  # the end of the output is the part that says why
313	            tail = tail.encode()[-CHECK_TAIL_BYTES:].decode("utf-8", "ignore")
314	        return f"exit {code}\n{tail}"

317	class Sandbox:
318	    """Where the world's tests run: a container, no network, the world mounted read-only.
319	
320	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the world's own locked dependencies,
321	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
322	    """
323	
324	    @staticmethod
325	    def image(world: Path) -> str:
326	        """The image name for this world: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
327	        h = hashlib.sha256((world / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (world / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
328	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
329	
330	    @staticmethod
331	    def ensure_image(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
332	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
333	        name = Sandbox.image(world)
334	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
335	        if seen.returncode == 0:
336	            return name
337	        built = subprocess.run(
338	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
339	            # factory never runs from inside the world.
340	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(world / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(world)],
341	            capture_output=True,
342	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
343	        )
344	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
345	        if built.returncode != 0:
346	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
347	        return name
348	
349	    @staticmethod
350	    def run(world: Path, run_dir: Path, n: int) -> tuple[int, str]:
351	        """The world's tests, once: the exit code and everything the run printed."""
352	        name = Sandbox.ensure_image(world, run_dir)
353	        container = f"factory-check-{run_dir.name}-{n}"
354	        argv = [
355	            "docker", "run", "--rm", "--name", container,
356	            "--network", "none",  # the check cannot reach the key, the provider or the internet
357	            "--user", f"{os.getuid()}:{os.getgid()}",
358	            "-e", "HOME=/tmp",
359	            "-e", "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1",  # the world is read-only; do not try to cache
360	            "-v", f"{world}:/w:ro", "-w", "/w",
361	            "--memory", "1g", "--cpus", "2", "--pids-limit", "256",
362	            name, *CHECK_CMD,
363	        ]  # fmt: skip
364	        try:
365	            done = subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True, timeout=CHECK_TIMEOUT)
366	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
367	            try:  # the check is over either way; a wedged daemon must not hang the run too
368	                subprocess.run(["docker", "kill", container], capture_output=True, timeout=30)
369	            except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
370	                pass
371	            return 124, f"timeout after {CHECK_TIMEOUT} s"
372	        # unittest writes to stderr; the world's own code may write to either.
373	        return done.returncode, (done.stdout + done.stderr).decode("utf-8", "replace")

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out
411	
412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),
439	        )

518	def dirty_paths(world: Path) -> list[str]:
519	    """The paths a git world has changed, staged or not, as git status names them. Read-only."""
520	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
521	    # Each entry is two status characters, a space, then the path; a rename adds the old path as

523	    return [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if len(entry) > 3 and entry[2] == " "]

526	def record_diff(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}
530	    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
531	    status = git(world, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
532	    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
533	    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too; before the first commit
534	    # there is no HEAD and a bare diff is all there is.
535	    head = subprocess.run(
536	        ["git", "-C", str(world), "rev-parse", "--verify", "-q", "HEAD"],
537	        capture_output=True,
538	        timeout=60,
539	    ).returncode == 0
540	    diff = ["diff", "HEAD"] if head else ["diff"]
541	    patch = [git(world, *diff)]
542	    for rel in untracked:
543	        patch.append(git(world, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
544	    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
545	    files = insertions = deletions = 0
546	    for line in git(world, *diff, "--numstat").splitlines():
547	        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)

1	# factory
2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. It is built one version at a time and its own repository is its first world: since v0.3 its code is written by `builder.py` itself, from tests written before each build, and v0.4 is the first version made that way. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. For each spec the attended agent writes the tests that name the seed, commits them red on a branch in a git worktree, and runs `builder.py` from the main checkout with that worktree as the world and the seed's goal as the goal. The factory writes the code. The attended agent reads the record and the diff, copies the record into the worktree, commits both as the factory's work, and when the review finds a defect turns it into a test and builds again. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}
```

317	class Sandbox:
318	    """Where the checkout's tests run: a container, no network, the checkout mounted read-only.
319	
320	    The only place that knows about Docker. The image is the checkout's own locked dependencies,
321	    built once per (uv.lock, check.Dockerfile) pair and reused by every run afterwards.
322	    """

324	    @staticmethod
325	    def image(checkout: Path) -> str:
326	        """The image name for this checkout: what it locks and how it is built, hashed."""
327	        h = hashlib.sha256((checkout / "uv.lock").read_bytes() + (checkout / "check.Dockerfile").read_bytes())
328	        return f"factory-check:{h.hexdigest()[:12]}"
329	
330	    @staticmethod
331	    def ensure_image(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> str:
332	        """Build the image if it is not there yet; the build is the one step with network."""
333	        name = Sandbox.image(checkout)
334	        seen = subprocess.run(["docker", "image", "inspect", name], capture_output=True)
335	        if seen.returncode == 0:
336	            return name
337	        built = subprocess.run(
338	            # -f absolute: docker resolves a relative -f against the caller's directory, and the
339	            # factory never runs from inside the checkout.
340	            ["docker", "build", "-f", str(checkout / "check.Dockerfile"), "-t", name, str(checkout)],
341	            capture_output=True,
342	            timeout=IMAGE_TIMEOUT,
343	        )
344	        (run_dir / "image-build.log").write_bytes(built.stdout + built.stderr)
345	        if built.returncode != 0:
346	            raise RuntimeError(f"docker build failed (exit {built.returncode}); see image-build.log")
347	        return name

352	        name = Sandbox.ensure_image(checkout, run_dir)

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
390	
391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out
411	
412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.

30	Weak self-improvement starts here: the world the builder edits is the factory's own repository.

36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). 39	- **Reference builder prompt.** mini-SWE-agent's system template is one sentence ("You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer."); the work lives in the instance message: the task, a numbered workflow (read relevant files, reproduce, edit, verify, edge cases, submit with an explicit command), and execution rules. Short, structured, task-adjacent, no persona.
40	
41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. 45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). Image `factory-check:<12 hex of sha256(uv.lock + check.Dockerfile)>` built once from `check.Dockerfile` (`python:3.12-slim`, `pip install` of `uv export --frozen --no-hashes`), with network; the check itself runs `docker run --rm --network none --user <uid>:<gid> -e HOME=/tmp -e PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 -v <world>:/w:ro -w /w --memory 1g --cpus 2 --pids-limit 256 <image> python -P -m unittest discover -q`, subprocess timeout 120 s then `docker kill` (30 s). `-P` keeps the world off `sys.path` while the standard runner is imported: without it a world-root `unittest.py` written by the model turns any suite green (review finding, reproduced in the real sandbox). The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.

38	- **Instructions.** `Agent(instructions=ROLE)`; instructions are re-sent each request and not stored as a message part (`system_prompt` would be). Nothing is appended to them in tool-output mode.
39	- **Tools.** `Agent(tools=[Tool(fn, takes_ctx=False), ...])`; schema from type hints + docstring (google/numpy/sphinx via griffe). Invalid arguments become a retry prompt to the model (budget `retries={'tools': 1}` default; exhaustion raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`). Unknown tool name → retry prompt "Unknown tool name: ... Available tools: ...".
40	- **Output.** `output_type=Report` (BaseModel) defaults to **tool output**: a synthetic tool `final_result` whose description is the model's docstring and whose parameters are its JSON schema; `tool_choice` forced to it when the profile allows. Plain text instead → retry prompt "Plain text responses are not permitted, please call one of the functions instead." (budget `retries={'output': 1}`).
41	- **Limits.** `UsageLimits(request_limit=50 default, tool_calls_limit=None, total_tokens_limit=None, cost_limit=None, ...)`; hitting one raises `UsageLimitExceeded`; no result survives, but messages do inside `with capture_run_messages() as messages:`.

The openai SDK retries 429/5xx twice on its own; `RunUsage.requests` counts logical requests, the wire log counts attempts.

50	2. **Cap hit = failed run, no forced report.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=40, request_limit=60)`. On `UsageLimitExceeded` the run records `stopped=cap`, keeps the messages via `capture_run_messages`, writes no report. Cleaner signal for evals than v0.1's "write it anyway", and avoids driving `agent.iter` by hand. Behaviour change vs v0.1, noted in README.
51	3. **Thinking at the API default, temperature 0, output retries 2.** Same request shape as v0.1 so the parity run measures the library swap only; gotcha 1 handled by the profile, not by disabling thinking. 380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()

387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text

404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )

428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),

526	def record_diff(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}

532	    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
533	    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too; before the first commit

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}
```

10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.

36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.

41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.
62	12. **Tags** `v0.3` at the merge. The factory's first build (G1 below) becomes `v0.4` after review, the first version built by the factory.

21	# Factory v0.2: the observer rebuilt on pydantic-ai
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	v0.1 (`/opt/yellow-robots/factory`, `main` at bc8eac0) is an owned loop of ~300 lines: fixed role text, two confined tools (`list`, `read`), DeepSeek over raw HTTP, a run record (`transcript.jsonl`, `response.md`, `numbers.json`). 26	
27	The owner's direction: do not build loop machinery from scratch; own the plane and the roles, borrow the loop from a library reviewed by many, pin it, read once what it adds. Pick: **pydantic-ai**. v0.2 is the observer rebuilt on it: same plane, near-identical role text, a typed four-field report, the same caps, run on the same goal and model as v0.1, compared against the v0.1 run. The swap is paid for when the differences are noise; if the library's additions change behaviour, it shows on one run before anything is built on top.
28	
29	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
30	
31	## Facts established (research, 2026-09-15)
32	
33	- **Package.** `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0` (released 2026-09-12; v2.0 was 2026-06-23). Core deps: `pydantic>=2.12`, `pydantic-graph`, `httpx2>=2.7` (Pydantic's httpx fork), `anyio`, `genai-prices`, `griffelib`, `opentelemetry-api`; the extra adds `openai>=3.8.0`, `tiktoken`. 34	- **Model.** `OpenAIChatModel('deepseek-flash', provider=DeepSeekProvider(api_key=..., http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(...)))`. Settings via `OpenAIChatModelSettings` (`temperature`, `seed`, `timeout`, `thinking`, ...).
35	- **Model name.** `deepseek-flash` is the current name and is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` is still accepted but retired (same model, Flash price). We use `deepseek-flash`, as v0.1 did.
36	- **Gotcha 1.** pydantic-ai's DeepSeek profile keys on the name string and treats only `deepseek-v4-*` as V4. For `deepseek-flash` it will therefore send a forced `tool_choice` for the output tool while the API has thinking on by default, which DeepSeek rejects with HTTP 400 ("Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice"). Fix, in order of preference: pass a merged `profile=` marking the model as thinking-capable with `openai_supports_forced_tool_choice_with_thinking=False` (tool choice becomes `auto`, thinking stays at the API default exactly as in v0.1, so the comparison isolates the library swap); fallback `thinking=False` in model settings if the model then answers in text more than the output retry budget tolerates.
37	- **Gotcha 2.** genai-prices has no `deepseek-flash` row, so `result.usage().cost` is `None`; keep our price table as fallback and record which source produced the number.
38	- **Instructions.** `Agent(instructions=ROLE)`; instructions are re-sent each request and not stored as a message part (`system_prompt` would be). Nothing is appended to them in tool-output mode.
39	- **Tools.** `Agent(tools=[Tool(fn, takes_ctx=False), ...])`; schema from type hints + docstring (google/numpy/sphinx via griffe). Invalid arguments become a retry prompt to the model (budget `retries={'tools': 1}` default; exhaustion raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`). Unknown tool name → retry prompt "Unknown tool name: ... Available tools: ...".
40	- **Output.** `output_type=Report` (BaseModel) defaults to **tool output**: a synthetic tool `final_result` whose description is the model's docstring and whose parameters are its JSON schema; `tool_choice` forced to it when the profile allows. 41	- **Limits.** `UsageLimits(request_limit=50 default, tool_calls_limit=None, total_tokens_limit=None, cost_limit=None, ...)`; hitting one raises `UsageLimitExceeded`; no result survives, but messages do inside `with capture_run_messages() as messages:`.

The openai SDK retries 429/5xx twice on its own; `RunUsage.requests` counts logical requests, the wire log counts attempts.
44	- **Tests.** `FunctionModel(fn)` with `fn(messages, info) -> ModelResponse`; `TestModel`; `models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`; `agent.override(model=...)`.

50	2. **Cap hit = failed run, no forced report.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=40, request_limit=60)`. function.name: list
function.description:
List one directory of the world: one entry per line as kind, size, path. Path is
relative to the world root; '.' is the root.

function.name: read
function.description:
Read a file of the world as numbered lines, from line `start` (1-based), at most 300
lines or 32000 bytes per call; a truncated read says where to continue.

path.description: The file to read, relative to the world root.

function.name: write
function.description:
Write a file of the world: create it, or replace what is there with `content`.

path.description: The file to write, relative to the world root.

content.description: The whole text of the file, as it should be afterwards.

function.name: edit
function.description:
Edit a file of the world: replace `old` with `new`, once. `old` must appear in the
file exactly once; if it does not, nothing is changed and the count is reported. The
tests and the toolchain cannot be edited.

path.description: The file to edit, relative to the world root.

old.description: The exact text to replace; include lines around it to make it unique.

new.description: The text to put in its place.

function.name: check
function.description:
Run the world's tests and return the exit code and the tail of the output: exit 0 is
green, anything else is red. The tests run in a container, with the world read-only and
no network, so this reports on the world as it is on disk. At most 8 checks per run.

changed.description: The paths you wrote or edited, in order.

did.description: What you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path.

check.description: Green or red: the state of the last check.

unsure.description: What you could not determine or verify.

379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )

391	    def _write(self, **entry: Any) -> None:
392	        with self.path.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
393	            f.write(json.dumps({"t": round(time.time(), 3), **entry}, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
394	
395	    @staticmethod
396	    def _body(text: str) -> Any:
397	        """A body that parses as JSON is recorded as the parsed value, so reading the record needs
398	        no second json.loads; a body that does not parse as JSON stays the text it was."""
399	        try:
400	            return json.loads(text)
401	        except ValueError:  # not JSON: keep the text, as the only thing it can be read as
402	            return text
403	
404	    def _headers(self, headers: Any) -> dict[str, str]:
405	        """Which headers were sent, never what the secret ones said."""
406	        out = {}
407	        for name, value in headers.items():
408	            name = name.lower()
409	            out[name] = "<redacted>" if name in SECRET_HEADERS else value
410	        return out

412	    async def on_request(self, request: Any) -> None:
413	        """Every attempt the SDK makes, headers and body included; the key is never written."""
414	        self.attempts += 1
415	        try:
416	            body = request.content.decode("utf-8", "replace")
417	        except Exception:  # a streamed body has nothing to record
418	            body = ""
419	        self._write(
420	            dir="request",
421	            method=request.method,
422	            url=str(request.url),
423	            status=None,
424	            headers=self._headers(request.headers),
425	            body=self._body(body),
426	        )
427	
428	    async def on_response(self, response: Any) -> None:
429	        """The answer to it, read in full so the body is there even when the SDK streams."""
430	        await response.aread()
431	        req = response.request
432	        self._write(
433	            dir="response",
434	            method=req.method,
435	            url=str(req.url),
436	            status=response.status_code,
437	            headers=self._headers(response.headers),
438	            body=self._body(response.text),

526	def record_diff(world: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
527	    """What the run left in the world: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
528	    if not (world / ".git").exists():  # a worktree has a .git file, a clone a .git directory
529	        return {"diff": "not a git checkout", "files_changed": 0, "insertions": 0, "deletions": 0}
530	    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.

532	    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
533	    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too; before the first commit
534	    # there is no HEAD and a bare diff is all there is.
535	    head = subprocess.run(

537	        capture_output=True,

2	
3	The factory is `builder.py`: a program that runs a cold model session over a directory, the world, until the world's tests pass, under walls the model cannot cross. What it can do is read off the records of its runs. Nothing in this repository is written for a model to obey; what holds is held by tests, by the plane, by the gate and by git.
4	
5	You are the attended agent: a model in some harness, resuming this work cold, working with the owner. This file is for any such model. The state of the work is never narrated here; it is derived from git and the files, as below.
6	
7	## Orient yourself
8	
9	Run these before reading anything else, from the root of the checkout or worktree you are in:
10	
11	```sh
12	uv run gate.py check                                               # the vault against its templates and the repository; silent when they agree
13	uv run python -m unittest -q                                       # the factory's tests; no provider, no network, no docker
14	git tag -l --format='%(refname:strip=2) %(objectname:short)'       # the released versions
15	git log --oneline "tags/$(git describe --tags --abbrev=0)..HEAD"   # what happened since the last one
16	git status --short                                                 # what is not committed; see the last section
17	ls docs/versions docs/seeds                                        # the versions and the backlog
18	ls runs | tail -3                                                  # the last run records
19	```
20	
21	Then derive:
22	
23	- The version in flight is the note in `docs/versions/` whose name is not a tag; there is at most one. Its seeds are the notes in `docs/seeds/` whose `version` names it.
24	- A seed's stage is its `status`. `open`: evidence and an idea. `spec`: a `## Goal` the builder can be given, assigned to a version. `building`: at least one test names it, `seed: <name>` in the test's docstring, committed red. `done`: merged and green. `rejected`: a way out at any stage. `docs/templates/seed.md` states what each status requires and the gate checks it; `docs/backlog.base` ranks the seeds.
25	- What the builder does and refuses is `README.md`; the walls are the constants at the top of `builder.py`; the exact behaviour is `test_builder.py`. The gate's is `test_gate.py`.
26	- A run is a directory under `runs/`: read `numbers.json` first (`stopped`, `check`, `world_head`, cost, counts), then `response.md`, `diff.patch` and `wire.jsonl`. The commit that took the diff names the run in its `Built-By` trailer, so the builds of a version are `git log --format='%h %(trailers:key=Built-By,valueonly)' tags/<previous>..tags/<version>`, and the run's `world_head` is the red commit it started from.
27	
28	## How a version is made
29	
30	The owner and the attended agent choose seeds from the backlog and promote them to specs: a version is assigned, the idea becomes a goal. def record_diff(checkout: Path, run_dir: Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """What the run left in the checkout: diff.patch, and the three numbers about it."""
    # -z so a path with a space or a quote survives; -uall so a new directory is listed as files.
    status = git(checkout, "status", "--porcelain", "-z", "--untracked-files=all")
    untracked = [entry[3:] for entry in status.split("\0") if entry.startswith("?? ")]
    # Against HEAD, so a change the run staged is in the patch too.
    patch = [git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD")]
    for rel in untracked:
        patch.append(git(checkout, "diff", "--no-index", "/dev/null", rel))
    (run_dir / "diff.patch").write_text("".join(patch))  # the patch first: counting can fail
    files = insertions = deletions = 0
    for line in git(checkout, "diff", "HEAD", "--numstat").splitlines():
        added, removed, _path = line.split("\t", 2)
        files += 1
        insertions += int(added) if added.isdigit() else 0  # "-" for a binary file
        deletions += int(removed) if removed.isdigit() else 0
    for rel in untracked:
        files += 1
        p = checkout / rel  # a broken symlink or a nested checkout has no lines to count
        insertions += len(p.read_bytes().splitlines()) if p.is_file() and not p.is_symlink() else 0
    return {"files_changed": files, "insertions": insertions, "deletions": deletions}
```

10	
11	- Five functions: `list`, `read`, `write` (create or replace, parents inside the world), `edit` (exactly one occurrence), `check` (the world's tests in a container, no network, world read-only, exit code and tail returned, full log kept). Every failure is an `error: ...` string.

22	# Factory v0.3: the builder
23	
24	## Context
25	
26	v0.2 (`main` 26eb3e8, tag `v0.2`) is the observer on pydantic-ai: a cold session that reads a world through `list` and `read` and returns a typed report; the record holds the wire, the messages and the numbers. It cannot act.
27	
28	v0.3 evolves the observer into the **builder**: the same loop, plane and record, with three more functions (`write`, `edit`, `check`), a world handed in as an argument, and a goal that is reached when the world's tests pass. From v0.3 on the factory is the builder: the attended agent plans, writes the spec and the red tests, creates the worktree and instantiates the factory; the factory does the one step in between; the attended agent reviews the diff, verifies, merges and tags. v0.3 itself is the last version built by agents, because v0.2 cannot write.

36	- **Host.** Docker 29.8.0, rootful daemon, apparmor + seccomp default profiles, `jbrey` in the `docker` group (root-equivalent on the host; the containers themselves run as `jbrey`'s uid). A tool that raises kills the run, a tool that returns a string is an ordinary result; `Literal` fields work in output models; `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit, request_limit)` raise `UsageLimitExceeded`; `capture_run_messages` keeps the history on any exception; `ModelSettings.extra_body` passes provider-specific body fields.

41	## Decisions (recommended; strike any you disagree with)
42	
43	1. **One role, one file.** `builder.py build <world> "<goal>"`? No: `builder.py <world> "<goal>"`. The observer role is not carried; the builder observes before it writes. A read-only role, if ever wanted again, is a role text plus a tool subset, not a program. Naming of files and roles evolves when there is more than one role.
44	2. **The world is an argument.** A directory, required to exist; in practice the worktree the attended agent hands in. The record lands under the factory's own `runs/`, outside the world by construction. `HIDDEN` at the world root as in v0.2 **plus `.git`** (review finding: a writable `.git/hooks` is model code running on the host the next time the human runs git there; the record's diff is made by the factory with the git binary and is unaffected).
45	3. **Five functions.** `list`, `read` as in v0.2; `write(path, content)` creates or overwrites a text file (parents created inside the world); `edit(path, old, new)` replaces exactly one occurrence of `old`, else returns an error naming the count; `check()` runs the world's tests in the sandbox and returns the exit code and the tail of the output. Every error is a returned `error: ...` string, never an exception. `check` is how the builder knows the goal is reached.
46	4. **Protected paths.** The plane refuses `write`/`edit` on `test*.py` (unittest's own discovery pattern, any depth), anything under `tests/`, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `check.Dockerfile`: the goal's criteria and the toolchain are the human's. Deterministic, tested, not prose.
47	5. **The goal.** Text passed on the command line (what and why, in a few sentences) plus the tests in the world. *Reached* is `check` green: every test passes, the human's red ones included, with no protected file touched. *Accepted* is the attended review of the diff against the goal's text, since green tests are a floor, not the spec. Nothing else defines it in v0.3.
48	6. **Check runs in a Docker container, world mounted read-only.** This sandboxes the check only; it is not how the factory is installed or run (that is a later version, undecided). The record's diff is `git diff HEAD` (staged changes included) with a `--no-index` diff per untracked file. The `Sandbox` class is the only place that knows Docker, so swapping to bubblewrap later is one class.
49	7. **Caps.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=80, request_limit=60)`; plane caps `CHECK_CAP = 8` and `WRITE_CAP = 30` (writes + edits), after which the function returns `error: cap reached ...; report now`. A cap hit in the library ends the run with no report, as in v0.2.
50	8. **The builder stops itself.** It calls `final_result` when check is green or when it gives up. The plane records the truth independently: `numbers.check` is the last check's exit code (`green`/`red`/`none`) next to the report's own `check` claim. A mismatch is a measure.
51	9. **The record grows by the diff.** After the run the factory runs `git diff` and `git status --porcelain` in the world (read-only git, not exposed to the model) and writes `diff.patch`; `check-<n>.log` per check; numbers add `world`, `writes`, `edits`, `checks`, `check`, `files_changed`, `insertions`, `deletions`, `check_seconds`.
52	10. **The prompt is a versioned instrument, not a belief.** Structure follows the reference: one short role sentence, the tools and what their results mean, a numbered order of work, the stopping rule, the report shape, a handful of rules. Its hash is in every record; changing it is a version; its effect is read off runs, which is how "does it matter" gets answered. No persona, no few-shot, no long rule lists. Text (fixed in `builder.py`):
53	
54	    > You are the builder. You are given a goal and a world: a directory with code and tests. You can explore it with `list` and `read`, change it with `write` and `edit`, and test it with `check`. The goal is reached when `check` is green: the tests are the goal's acceptance criteria and cannot be changed.
55	    >
56	    > Work in this order: read what the goal touches; run `check` once to see what fails; make the smallest change that can make it pass; run `check`; repeat. Stop when `check` is green, or when you cannot make it green within the budget, and return the report through the `final_result` function: changed (the paths you wrote or edited, in order), did (what you changed and why, one fact per item, each naming a path), check (green or red), failing (test names if red), unsure (what you could not determine or verify).
57	    >
58	    > Rules: change only what the goal needs; prefer `edit` over `write` for existing files; never work around a failing test by changing what it asserts; no commentary outside the report.
59	
60	    Output model `BuildReport(changed: list[str], did: list[str], check: Literal["green", "red"], failing: list[str], unsure: list[str])`, rendered to `response.md` as five sections.
61	11. **Model settings tell the truth.** `temperature` is dropped (no effect in thinking mode); thinking stays at the API default; `timeout` 180 s. Numbers keep `reasoning_tokens`.
62	12. **Tags** `v0.3` at the merge. The factory's first build (G1 below) becomes `v0.4` after review, the first version built by the factory.

21	# Factory v0.2: the observer rebuilt on pydantic-ai
22	
23	## Context
24	
25	v0.1 (`/opt/yellow-robots/factory`, `main` at bc8eac0) is an owned loop of ~300 lines: fixed role text, two confined tools (`list`, `read`), DeepSeek over raw HTTP, a run record (`transcript.jsonl`, `response.md`, `numbers.json`). 26	
27	The owner's direction: do not build loop machinery from scratch; own the plane and the roles, borrow the loop from a library reviewed by many, pin it, read once what it adds. Pick: **pydantic-ai**. v0.2 is the observer rebuilt on it: same plane, near-identical role text, a typed four-field report, the same caps, run on the same goal and model as v0.1, compared against the v0.1 run. The swap is paid for when the differences are noise; if the library's additions change behaviour, it shows on one run before anything is built on top.
28	
29	Self-contained version: a cold agent gets this plan and the repository, nothing else.
30	
31	## Facts established (research, 2026-09-15)
32	
33	- **Package.** `pydantic-ai-slim[openai]==2.43.0` (released 2026-09-12; v2.0 was 2026-06-23). Core deps: `pydantic>=2.12`, `pydantic-graph`, `httpx2>=2.7` (Pydantic's httpx fork), `anyio`, `genai-prices`, `griffelib`, `opentelemetry-api`; the extra adds `openai>=3.8.0`, `tiktoken`. 34	- **Model.** `OpenAIChatModel('deepseek-flash', provider=DeepSeekProvider(api_key=..., http_client=httpx2.AsyncClient(...)))`. Settings via `OpenAIChatModelSettings` (`temperature`, `seed`, `timeout`, `thinking`, ...).
35	- **Model name.** `deepseek-flash` is the current name and is served by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash; the legacy `deepseek-v4-flash` is still accepted but retired (same model, Flash price). We use `deepseek-flash`, as v0.1 did.
36	- **Gotcha 1.** pydantic-ai's DeepSeek profile keys on the name string and treats only `deepseek-v4-*` as V4. For `deepseek-flash` it will therefore send a forced `tool_choice` for the output tool while the API has thinking on by default, which DeepSeek rejects with HTTP 400 ("Thinking mode does not support this tool_choice"). Fix, in order of preference: pass a merged `profile=` marking the model as thinking-capable with `openai_supports_forced_tool_choice_with_thinking=False` (tool choice becomes `auto`, thinking stays at the API default exactly as in v0.1, so the comparison isolates the library swap); fallback `thinking=False` in model settings if the model then answers in text more than the output retry budget tolerates.
37	- **Gotcha 2.** genai-prices has no `deepseek-flash` row, so `result.usage().cost` is `None`; keep our price table as fallback and record which source produced the number.
38	- **Instructions.** `Agent(instructions=ROLE)`; instructions are re-sent each request and not stored as a message part (`system_prompt` would be). Nothing is appended to them in tool-output mode.
39	- **Tools.** `Agent(tools=[Tool(fn, takes_ctx=False), ...])`; schema from type hints + docstring (google/numpy/sphinx via griffe). Invalid arguments become a retry prompt to the model (budget `retries={'tools': 1}` default; exhaustion raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior`). Unknown tool name → retry prompt "Unknown tool name: ... Available tools: ...".
40	- **Output.** `output_type=Report` (BaseModel) defaults to **tool output**: a synthetic tool `final_result` whose description is the model's docstring and whose parameters are its JSON schema; `tool_choice` forced to it when the profile allows. 41	- **Limits.** `UsageLimits(request_limit=50 default, tool_calls_limit=None, total_tokens_limit=None, cost_limit=None, ...)`; hitting one raises `UsageLimitExceeded`; no result survives, but messages do inside `with capture_run_messages() as messages:`.

The openai SDK retries 429/5xx twice on its own; `RunUsage.requests` counts logical requests, the wire log counts attempts.
44	- **Tests.** `FunctionModel(fn)` with `fn(messages, info) -> ModelResponse`; `TestModel`; `models.ALLOW_MODEL_REQUESTS = False`; `agent.override(model=...)`.

50	2. **Cap hit = failed run, no forced report.** `UsageLimits(tool_calls_limit=40, request_limit=60)`. 379	class Wire:
380	    """The raw HTTP record: one line per attempt, request and response, with no secret in it."""
381	
382	    def __init__(self, path: Path, transport: Any = None):
383	        self.path = path
384	        self.attempts = 0
385	        path.touch()
386	        self.client = httpx2.AsyncClient(
387	            transport=transport,
388	            event_hooks={"request": [self.on_request], "response": [self.on_response]},
389	        )
